checks.name: focused_frontend_tests
checks.detail: Four test files, 14 tests passed. Fakes exercise explicit enable, denied/revoked permission, generic DM preview, hidden-tab delivery, cross-tab event deduplication and silence for an unaddressed DM. These are source-level tests, not OS notification observations.

checks.name: third_participant_realtime_delivery
checks.detail: Previously authenticated third browser socket received zero DM create/edit/delete frames while the recipient received one of each. The current preflight did not repeat this browser experiment.

checks.name: browser_permission_and_os_notification
checks.detail: Chrome tab control could not load the browser request-header policy in repeated attempts; the in-app browser had no tab. No permission prompt was accepted, no hidden-tab system notification was observed, and neither generic preview nor cross-tab dedup was verified in an actual browser.

checks.name: isolated_in_app_browser_capability_probe
checks.detail: A localhost-only static server was started on port 18798 to inspect Notification API and permission read-only. Creating an in-app browser tab returned Browser is not available: iab; a fresh browser inventory listed only Chrome. No page or permission state was read. The local server was stopped.

remaining_condition: Use an accessible fixed or trusted browser bundle with two independent synthetic participant sessions and a third nonparticipant; grant notification permission in that test origin through the approved browser UI, hide the recipient tab, send a DM, and observe exactly one generic OS notification across two recipient tabs and none for the third account. Revoke permission and verify silence. Keep DM bodies and credentials out of evidence.
